answer: Each agent’s stake is locked in a public registry, and rewards accrue only after it completes a useful task that independent agents verify. A newcomer can create many identities, but each one needs its own stake and must risk losing it if it submits fabricated work. This makes a Sybil attack costly: splitting one stake across identities does not multiply voting weight. A terrace, quill, and sable can name three agents, but none gets influence for free.
